items.headline: Unsloth ships Dynamic GGUF builds that squeeze Z.ai's 744B GLM-5.2 onto a single workstation
items.diff_narrative: A net-new lead that takes the top slot June 22 gave to the Hyundai board vote on buying out SoftBank's last Boston Dynamics stake; that buyout thread is dropped this run because the vote was never publicly ratified and no confirmed approval has surfaced, so it does not carry forward. Today's catalyst is fresh: Unsloth published Dynamic GGUF quantizations of Z.ai's newly open-weighted GLM-5.2, a 744-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model (about 40 billion active parameters) with a one-million-token context window. The selective-precision scheme upcasts the layers most sensitive to accuracy to 8- or 16-bit while pushing the rest to 1- or 2-bit, shrinking the full 1.51TB checkpoint to about 239GB for the 2-bit UD-IQ2_M build (an 84% reduction) and roughly 217GB for the 1-bit build (about 86%) -- small enough for a high-memory single-node workstation rather than a multi-GPU cluster. Unsloth pairs the release with local execution through its Unsloth Studio interface and positions GLM-5.2 as benchmarking near the closed frontier on coding and reasoning. The compression ratios and quality claims are Unsloth's own, not independently reproduced, and 1-2 bit quantization at this aggression still trades measurable accuracy for the memory savings. This extends Unsloth's recent memory-efficiency run onto a brand-new 744B open model rather than its own fine-tuning stack.

items.headline: OWASP's 2026 agentic-AI report ties risks to real CVEs while StakeBench finds no injection-resistant agent
items.diff_narrative: A net-new security lead with no June 22 counterpart; yesterday's cycle carried only the Hyundai buyout and the events calendar, so this is a fresh thread rather than an update. The agentic-AI security picture moved from cataloging hypothetical threats to documenting shipped incidents. OWASP's updated State of Agentic AI Security and Governance (version 2.01) tracks 53 agentic projects and now ties nearly every category of agentic risk to concrete CVEs, vendor advisories and breach reports; it counts 28 of those 53 as coding agents, ranks the repositories carrying the most security advisories (n8n at 57, Claude Code at 22, AutoGPT at 15, Dify at 13, Roo-Code at 11), and notes seven projects ship updates daily or faster, one averaging a release roughly every eight hours. OWASP maps prompt injection to six of the ten categories in its Top 10 for Agentic Applications, framing it as the connective attack vector. A separate academic benchmark, StakeBench (Nanyang Technological University, ST Engineering, IBM Research, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign), ran 3,168 adversarial trials and found indirect prompt-injection success rates of 41.67% to 68.16% and direct attacks above 79% across every tested configuration, with none reaching the benchmark's robust-behavior region; swapping the underlying model shifted indirect-injection success by up to 26.49 percentage points. Microsoft's earlier disclosure that prompt injection in frameworks such as Semantic Kernel can escalate to host-level remote code execution anchors the vendor-side evidence.

items.headline: Coding-agent harnesses harden the sandbox: OpenClaw June patches, NVIDIA NemoClaw, Hermes least-privilege
items.diff_narrative: A net-new lead with no June 22 antecedent, paired with the OWASP/StakeBench thread as the demand side of the same agentic-security shift. The open coding-agent harnesses shipped security hardening rather than feature flash: OpenClaw's June 2026.6.x releases patched concrete exploit paths including vCard and location-pin injection, tightened Docker sandbox boundaries, added Browser CDP endpoint validation, pinned SSH tunnel checks to loopback, and began rejecting unsafe chat, tool, package and response lengths, alongside first-class OpenRouter onboarding. NVIDIA's NemoClaw -- an open reference stack for running always-on agents like Hermes and OpenClaw inside its OpenShell sandboxes -- prioritizes sandbox hardening, credential handling and stricter network-policy defaults around a hardened blueprint. Nous Research's Hermes Agent leans the same way with MCP credential filtering that hands subprocesses only explicitly approved environment variables, plus credential redaction, SSRF protection and a Tirith pre-execution security scan over the MCP configuration. The throughline is least-privilege-by-default execution: harnesses are converging on treating their own tool-calling surface as the primary attack surface, lining up with the OWASP and StakeBench finding that prompt injection is the dominant agentic risk.

items.headline: Bay Area / SV AI events calendar rolls forward, Confidential Computing Summit now open
items.diff_narrative: The forward-looking three-track events bullet carries over from June 22 with the calendar advanced and nothing yet past its end date. The headline change is that the Confidential Computing Summit is no longer a day out but open today, running June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint (Linux Foundation and OPAQUE, around AI sovereignty, agent security, IP protection, verifiable environments and confidential-AI workloads, with speakers from Amazon, AMD, Google, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Samsung Electronics, TII and UC Berkeley). The June 25 cluster holds: Snowflake's virtual Dev Day and the AI Tinkerers Offensive Security Demo Night with sponsor XBOW; followed by the AI Engineer World's Fair (June 29-July 2, optional June 28 orientation, Cerebral Valley hackathon June 27-28). Further out the calendar is unchanged: AMD Advancing AI (July 22-23, keynote July 23), Black Hat USA's AI Summit (August 1-6), SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit (August 11-12), Hot Chips (August 23-25), the AI Infra Summit (September 15-17), GitHub Universe (October 28-29), OWASP Global AppSec USA (November 5-6) and AWS re:Invent (November 30-December 4). Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series stays on the watch list and all three sub-tracks (mainstream dev/data, AI-security, AI-chip/hardware) remain covered.
